The Decoder - Alibaba's Qwen4-Max takes on Opus 5.5, GPT-6, and Kimi K3.1 Pro at much lower prices (2026-11-16)

attrs.summary: Alibaba released Qwen4-Max, a mixture-of-experts model with 2.4 trillion total parameters activating about 71 billion per token, processing images natively and offering a one-million-token context window. Its revamped Qwen4 architecture compresses the prior context across three layers while a fourth layer selects only the relevant parts, adds four parallel layer connections with dynamic gates, and introduces a 328-billion-parameter N-gram embedding layer of ready-made token sequences, which Alibaba says let the 2.4T configuration train stably with no loss spikes. On internal bits-per-byte evaluation across knowledge, code, QA and STEM, Qwen4-Max-Base improved 5 to 13 percent over Qwen3.8-Max-Base while activating 25 percent fewer parameters per token. On the Work360 industrial benchmark covering 721 specialized fields, Qwen4-Max uses roughly a quarter to a third fewer tokens than its predecessor, the average cost per task falls 62 percent from $4.43 to $1.67, and the score climbs from 47.74 to 52.69; on Terminal-Bench 4.0 token use drops by nearly half with a 48 percent score. On long-horizon agent tasks it scores 46.7 on Agents' Last Exam v1.1, the best in its comparison group, but it trails Opus 5.5 and the GPT models on Humanity's Last Exam and the GPT models on HealthBench Professional. On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index it scores 43 at highest reasoning, nine points above Qwen3.8-Max and three behind Kimi K3.1 Pro, at a cost of $3.27 per task versus $10.02 for its predecessor and $3.68 for Kimi, using roughly 105,000 output tokens per benchmark task against 171,000. Alibaba charges $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million output tokens, with cache hits at $0.075. Tencent's Hy4 is much cheaper at $1.03 per task but scores eight points lower. The release also adds a Live Delivery feature that lets users inspect intermediate results from autonomous agents and adjust running tasks.

The Decoder - Claude now builds interactive websites inside canvas graphics, reviving the Flash era with real HTML (2026-11-16)

attrs.summary: Claude can now embed text, buttons and other web elements into complex graphics and 3D effects through HTML-in-Canvas, which places real page elements inside canvas graphics while keeping them fully interactive. Standard HTML elements are clickable, selectable and readable by screen readers but are hard to warp visually, while canvas can draw anything but the browser treats it as a flat image whose text cannot be selected and whose links cannot be clicked. Felix Rieseberg, who works on Claude at Anthropic, wrote on X that Claude can now build bizarre and beautiful sites with the feature and that it reminds him of the Flash era. A demo page shows 15 examples including websites rendered as knitting patterns, 3D cubes or exploded layer views, with content remaining real selectable text. Google is developing HTML-in-Canvas as a web standard preserving both interactivity and accessibility. The feature works in Chrome and Edge from version 157 and in Claude desktop apps from version 5.11492, while Safari and Firefox do not support it yet, and users must ask Claude for HTML-in-Canvas explicitly in the prompt.

nodes.label: The Decoder - Anthropic says the key to agent memory is knowing what to forget, not how much to store (2026-11-16)

attrs.summary: Anthropic researched how Claude retains knowledge across sessions while the model itself stays unchanged, with Claude writing notes to a folder it can read back later. The core problem is selection: before the agent knows what comes next it must decide in the moment what might matter later, so every note is a bet on the future. In a test with Pokemon Red, Claude Sonnet 3.7 treated everything as potentially important and across roughly 10,000 game steps created 413 files in 225 folders, often one per battle and item, and because game state keeps changing the archive goes stale fast; at times the model did nothing but reorganize its notes instead of playing and it finished with a single badge. The newer Claude Fable 5 limited memory to a few files, did not record information already visible on screen, wrote down plans, strategies and tested rules, and earned four badges, though Anthropic notes the comparison covers only a single playthrough per model. Anthropic recommends explaining the purpose of memory to Claude and letting the model decide how to use it, because rigid instructions such as only record mistakes wiped out most of the advantage for stronger models, while older models benefited from explicit instructions such as being told to actually read their notes before every response. Anthropic introduced Dreaming in May as a research preview for Claude Managed Agents, where the service reads an existing memory store and up to 100 past sessions, removes duplicate and outdated entries and creates a reorganized store while leaving the original untouched, initially supporting only Claude Opus 4.7 and Sonnet 4.6. OpenAI also calls the ChatGPT memory it overhauled in June Dreaming and reports it raised temporal accuracy from 52.2 to 75.1 percent, and Google and Google DeepMind researchers use dreaming differently, to improve an agent search strategy by working through alternative solutions using already stored results without calling the model again. Anthropic warns that taking notes mid-task distracts the agent, that Dreaming costs extra compute and returns results only after a delay, and that wikis and notes need regular upkeep or errors and hallucinations accumulate.

nodes.label: Google AI blog RSS recovered after 10 empty windows (2026-11-17)

attrs.summary: The Google AI blog RSS feed had returned a 299-byte redirect shell for ten consecutive NightOps windows, and the window reports had repeatedly recommended removing the source from the collection list. This window root-caused it instead of dropping it: blog.google/technology/ai/rss/ does not serve the feed directly, it returns an HTTP 302 redirect to blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/ai/rss/, and the collection script used curl without -L, so only the redirect body was ever captured. Following the redirect returns HTTP 200 with 30,392 bytes and 20 items, the newest being New Ask Maps features to help with holiday travel and prep dated 2026-11-16, followed by Google Search gets a major upgrade with Gemini 4 Hydrogen on 2026-11-12, Gemini Decisions API: Fast, calibrated multimodal decisions on 2026-11-11, and Gemini Intelligence: New features, on more devices on 2026-11-10. The fetch script was patched to add -L, which also protects the arXiv, HackerNews and RSS calls in the same script from the same class of silent failure. The signal content is worth more than the fix itself: the recovered feed carries Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a Gemini Decisions API for calibrated multimodal decisions and a Gemini Intelligence feature expansion, which is the Google-side counterpart to the Qwen4-Max and Anthropic memory stories in the same window.

nodes.label: The Decoder - Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 doesn't generate images, it paints them (2026-11-15)

attrs.summary: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 generates images not with a diffusion model but by writing a 1,000 to 2,000 line Python program that drives a simulated paint engine placing brushstrokes on a virtual canvas, simulating bristle texture, paint application and mistakes it later paints over. Developer Jake Eaton showed a photorealistic shopping cart in a parking garage built from roughly 700,000 simulated brushstrokes, and a bird painting from 111 coordinate sequences, with deviations corrected after the fact. On Anthropic internal RoboDojo Sim benchmark Fable 5.2 scored 64.9 percent versus 29.8 percent for OpenAI GPT-6 Astra, but it lagged its rival in speed and in fine motor control in a real-world test with a physical robot arm. Unlike the sibling Opus 5.5, which was criticized for imitating existing art, Fable 5.2 develops its own artist personas with fictional backstories and consistent styles, and the developer redirects it with comments mid-stroke. The approach resembles agentic image editing where a language model picks tools and evaluates results, and it marks a shift from pixel-space generation to program-space generation for image synthesis.

nodes.label: The Decoder - Meituan releases a 1.6-trillion-parameter agent model that never touched an Nvidia GPU (2026-11-15)

attrs.summary: Meituan's LongCat team released weights for LongCat-2.5, a 1.6-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model built for autonomous long multi-step agent tasks, especially coding, and trained entirely on Chinese hardware. Roughly 48 billion parameters are active per token, it handles up to one million tokens in context and generates up to 128,000 tokens, it understands text, images and video by converting images into discrete tokens at native resolution rather than bolting on a separate image encoder, and it lets users toggle reasoning. It performs at the level of models like Claude Opus 5 reached a few months earlier on coding benchmarks. For reinforcement learning the team used real software tasks from GitHub pull requests plus recreated agent failures, blocked internet access, removed Git history and cached files, and had a language model check solutions for shortcuts, and it distilled capabilities from several specialized teacher models. Meituan quantizes expert weights and activations to 4-bit precision, which Chinese chips process natively, and load tests show throughput up 43.3 percent for prompt processing and 42.77 percent for response generation over an 8-bit version, with a sample deployment running on 194 Huawei chips.

nodes.label: The Decoder - Anthropic CEO Amodei admits huge uncertainty ahead of a record IPO (2026-11-14)

attrs.summary: Speaking at a JPMorgan Chase investor event in New York, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called buying compute the deepest business dilemma the company faces, warning that compute must be purchased one to two years ahead of knowing whether revenue will justify the cost, so buying too little hurts revenue while buying too much means financially overextending. The admission came days before Anthropic planned a Nov. 19 IPO that could be the largest in history. Anthropic has already committed nearly $901 billion, mostly to compute and chips according to Bloomberg, with roughly $71 billion due by September 2027, a figure exceeding the market cap of about two-thirds of S&P 500 companies. The IPO is designed to build a cash buffer large enough to carry the company through a potential mismatch between spending and revenue. Back in February 2026 Amodei had warned in sharper terms that he could buy $1 trillion of compute starting at the end of 2027. The window therefore contains a concrete exposure figure for agent economics: frontier lab compute commitments are now measured in hundreds of billions of dollars against uncertain monetization.

The Decoder - Australia central bank finds AI hitting young workers first (2026-11-15)

attrs.summary: An analysis by Mike Major for the Reserve Bank of Australia built a monitoring system focused on entry-level workers and highly AI-exposed occupations such as programming, clerical work and customer service. Job postings have fallen across all groups since ChatGPT launched in late 2022, with the steepest drop in the highest-exposure group, where workers aged 15 to 24 and young college graduates show weaker employment rates and higher unemployment than older workers, while employment among older workers in the same quintile has risen. Major cautions that the study establishes no direct causation and measures theoretical exposure rather than actual company use, and that post-pandemic business-cycle and remote-work shifts could also drive the numbers. Similar patterns appear in an August 2025 Stanford study of millions of US payroll records, where employment among 22 to 25 year olds in AI-exposed occupations fell 13 percent in relative terms since late 2022 and nearly 20 percent among young software developers, and in a March 2026 Anthropic study showing job-finding rates down about 14 percent for the same cohort with no systematic rise in overall unemployment. Anthropic internal review data cited in the piece shows junior hires in technical roles falling from 27 percent to 9 percent since early 2025, with AI agents across the company logging six times as many hours as human staff by August 2026.

The Decoder - Firm linked to Jensen Huang ex-lover brokered nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for China (2026-11-15)

attrs.summary: According to documents reviewed by the Wall Street Journal, Megaspeed arranged nearly $12 billion of Nvidia high-performance chip orders for Chinese companies between March 2024 and June 2025. Megaspeed is owned by Alice Huang, the former lover of since-ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and shipped chips to Chinese buyers with long-standing ties to local tech giants, covering several hundred thousand chips the US had sought to keep out of China through export controls. Megaspeed reportedly gained preferential access to scarce AI chips as an Nvidia cloud partner, apparently because it counted Alibaba as a major client. Nvidia officially reported $12.4 billion in China revenue over six months, 7 percent of total, while short-selling firm Culper Research estimates more than 20 percent of Nvidia revenue in the last fiscal year came from Chinese customers, so a significant share may have flowed through indirect channels. An update notes Megaspeed said Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang officially left the company on August 30, 2025 and has no current role, that she became controlling shareholder in March 2023 per Washington-based research group C4ADS, and that the company said it conducted legitimate and lawful business and retained external counsel for an internal investigation. Speculation that Huang may be a Chinese spy remains unconfirmed.
